v1.feedback: Strong piece — Lucy's silhouette reads immediately, the ivory-amber-ember-rose palette is restrained and warm, and the 12s volley cycle with 6s initial delay feels genuinely contemplative. Two refinements: reduce flutter amplitudes from 0.35 to ~0.18 so airborne petals drift rather than wiggle (current values border on busy for a 'gentle' intent), and consider dropping the volley fraction from 30% to ~18-20% per cycle so each exhale reads as a delicate sigh rather than a sneeze. A single slow camera dolly (e.g. z 30→28 over 60s) would add cinematic depth without violating the still-camera spirit.

v2.feedback: Strong concept — Lucy exhaling petals is a genuine creative swerve on the point-cloud parent, and the petal fragment shader (elongated ellipse with pinched base and vein line) is a nice tactile detail. Two refinements: (1) the volley particles grow via gl_PointSize scaling, but real petal drift would benefit from a slight downward curl at the trajectory's apex — add a small negative-y gravity term after peak detach to make the fall read as organic rather than pure linear drift; (2) the 0.18 selection fraction is uniform random, so petals detach evenly across the whole body — biasing volleySelect toward the torso/shoulder normals (e.g., weighting particles whose rest normal has a positive y component) would make the exhale read as rising from the chest, reinforcing the 'stone breathes' intent.
